$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the only one that exercises the scope control ground-truth.json
records under negativeControls. The verdict names a file that was never under review, and both the
harness scorer and the contract's scope oracle have to call that a false positive. Before this case
the rule was declared twice and scored nowhere: such a finding landed in unattributed, the bucket for
findings a human has yet to rule on, and this one needs no ruling.
derivation: The verdict carries ten findings: the nine planted rows at their firing lines, and an M6 against
src/orders.service.ts:14, the implementation the seeded spec imports and nobody asked the reviewer to
read. All ten name a file, so unlocated is 0 and reported is 10. The nine plants each find their
finding, so hits is 9, criticalHits 4 of 4, and misses is empty.
The M6 matches no plant. Its file ends in none of the three review-set basenames, so it is neither a
seeded fixture nor the clean control: it is out of scope. outOfScope is 1, and because an out-of-scope
finding is a definite false positive, falsePositives is 1 as well. Nothing lands in unattributed,
which is reserved for findings on a seeded fixture that match no plant.
The counts the harness derives from these: recall 9/9 = 1.00, CRITICAL recall 4/4 = 1.00,
nonFalsePositiveRate (10 - 1)/10 = 0.90 against a 0.80 floor. Counting the finding as unattributed
instead would give 10/10 = 1.00, which is the difference this case exists to pin.
score and recommendation come from the verdict: 100 - 4x10 - 4x5 - 1x2 - 1x1 = 37, Block on Criticals.
